source_title: Ferrari fastest as Verstappen says Kiwi rival should 'act a little smarter'
source_excerpt:
Charles Leclerc was the fastest of all drivers on Friday in Mexico City. ( Reuters: Eloisa Sanchez )
Ferrari's Charles Leclerc has finished fastest in both practice sessions on Friday, local time, ahead of this weekend's Formula 1 Mexican Grand Prix.
Max Verstappen and former teammate Liam Lawson collided.
ABC Sport will have a live blog of the Formula 1 Mexico City Grand Prix on Monday, November 2, from 5:30am AEDT.
Ferrari's Charles Leclerc was fastest in both practice sessions for a Mexico City Grand Prix set to crown 20-year-old Mercedes driver Kimi Antonelli as Formula 1's youngest champion.
Antonelli missed Thursday's media day to recover from a viral illness, but the Italian was second on the time sheets in the first session and fourth in the later one at the capital's high-altitude Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez.
Antonelli is 123 points clear of teammate George Russell at the top and needs only two more points, a ninth place, to be sure of the title while the Briton has to win on Sunday to stay mathematically in the game with four rounds remaining.
Leclerc, who was also fastest in both Friday sessions in Texas last week before Antonelli won, produced a best effort of 1:17.827 in the second practice, when the times were much closer, after going top in the first by 0.659 with a lap of 1:18.128.
"Overall, our performance looks quite all right, but we still need to work on some of our limiting factors. It was quite tricky on track today, as the surface was slippery," Leclerc said.
McLaren's reigning world champion and last year's winner, Lando Norris, was second fastest in the later session, 0.103 slower, with Russell third.
Leclerc's teammate and seven-time champion Lewis Hamilton, a two-time winner in Mexico, stopped on track and triggered a virtual safety car with half an hour remaining. "I lost all power," Hamilton said.
Red flags were shown and the session halted after Red Bull's Max Verstappen, a five-time winner in Mexico, and Racing Bulls' Liam Lawson, a former teammate, made contact with 47 minutes to go, leaving debris from the Dutch driver's car on the track.
"He literally just drove into me. Every weekend," Lawson said over the radio.
Verstappen hit back at the New Zealander, whose place has yet to be confirmed for next year.
"At the end of the day, it is not going to change my weekend, but if I were him I would act a little smarter. And when you're fighting for your seat, it's not very smart behaviour," he said.
ABC Sport will have a live blog of the Formula 1 Mexico City Grand Prix on Monday, November 2, from 5:30am AEDT.
